subject.title: Feature: configPatch in plugin manifest — automatic config setup on install

question: Should OpenClaw support third-party manifest-declared install-time config mutation, and if so should it be an allowlisted config-intent contract rather than arbitrary raw deep-merge patches?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but accepting plugin metadata that mutates persistent user config affects security, auth/provider routing, config data loss, and upgrade expectations; automation cannot choose that trust boundary safely.

options.title: Design allowlisted config intent
options.body: Define a constrained manifest contract with allowed config surfaces, validation, diff/skip UX, provenance, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Reject install-time mutation
options.body: Keep plugin install limited to plugin state and require setup/auth/doctor flows or manual `openclaw config patch` commands for broader config changes.

options.title: Accept raw configPatch
options.body: Allow arbitrary manifest deep-merge patches during install, accepting higher config and security risk for plugin setup convenience.

recommendation.title: Design allowlisted config intent
recommendation.body: Define a constrained manifest contract with allowed config surfaces, validation, diff/skip UX, provenance, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent live path history points most strongly to plugin manifest/install implementation ownership across the central files.
